subject: general
question: In which year did India officially start economic liberalisation?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1991**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• India officially started economic liberalisation in **1991** under the leadership of then Prime Minister **P.V. Narasimha Rao** and Finance Minister **Dr. Manmohan Singh**.
 
• The liberalisation measures were introduced to tackle the **balance of payments crisis** that India faced during the early 1990s.
 
• The reforms consisted of structural changes such as reducing trade barriers, deregulating industries, and encouraging foreign investment to spur economic growth.
 
• The **New Economic Policy (NEP)** of 1991 focused on **LPG: Liberalisation, Privatisation, and Globalisation**.
 
• Key sectors such as banking, telecommunications, and insurance experienced deregulation, and India opened its markets to global trade, marking a shift from a closed economy to a more market-oriented economy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: 1995**

 
 
• India joined the **World Trade Organization (WTO)** in 1995, which further integrated the Indian economy into global trade networks.
 
• The establishment of the WTO marked India's commitment to multilateral trade agreements and globalisation.
 
 
 
• **Option 2: 2000**
 
 
• During this period, India witnessed the **dot-com boom** and increased focus on the Information Technology (IT) sector, with IT industries becoming major contributors to economic growth.
 
• The **Electricity Act of 2003**, formulated shortly after this period, marked reforms in India's power sector.
 
 
 
• **Option 3: 1985**
 
 
• It marked preliminary steps towards reform under Prime Minister **Rajiv Gandhi**.
 
• During this time, there was an emphasis on promoting **technology and modernisation**, but comprehensive liberalisation measures were not introduced.
